disclosure: General behavioral-pricing pattern (the decoy effect) rather than a specific unverified metric or report figure.

claims.text: Most home service pros still hand customers a single price rather than tiered options.
Presenting three pricing tiers instead of one tends to increase how often customers say yes and how much they spend, compared to a single price.

When given three pricing options, customers tend to choose the middle tier rather than the cheapest or most expensive option, a widely documented pattern in pricing research known as the decoy effect.
